text:
Maria: Heads-up — I observed a client POST that was streaming a long upload. Edge retried mid-stream after a transient backend failure and we ended up with duplicate side-effects. We don't currently attach an idempotency key for streaming POSTs.
Sam: Ouch. Do we know why the edge retried instead of failing the request? Any partial body semantics?
Maria: It sent an early FIN from upstream, edge treated as transient network error and retried from scratch. Client resumed streaming but server processed both.
Kevin: This is the classic streaming POST + retry mismatch. Options: 1) enforce idempotency keys for any non-chunked POSTs, 2) make retries only safe for GET/PUT with idempotency, 3) add a resume token protocol for mid-stream restart.
Olivia: Agree. We also need to consider SLOs — if we disable retries for streams we lose automatic latency mitigation. Maybe differentiate by Content-Type and side-effect header?
Jun: Metric-wise: this pattern has been rare but high-severity. We have 12 incidents this month where a duplicate DB write occurred. We should track "edge.retries.streams.duplicate" as a counter.
Maria: I'm leaning toward: require explicit header `X-Redwood-Stream-Id` and `Idempotency-Key` for any streaming POST that can mutate state. If missing, edge refuses retry and propagates 5xx back. Safer default.
Sam: Sounds reasonable. Implementation notes: need a short TTL for Stream-Id -> backend mapping and a lightweight lease so backends can dedupe. Also document SDK helpers.
Kevin: For resume tokens: the server can emit a JSON trailer like `{ "resume_after": 12345 }` and the client can send `Resume-From: 12345` on retry. That requires support in our proxy to hydrate the partial KV cache. More intrusive.
Olivia: And tricky with third-party upstreams. I don't want the edge to try complex stateful resume for arbitrary backends.
Jun: Suggest split path: (A) For Redwood-managed backends we can support resume tokens and safe hedging; (B) For external upstreams, require `Idempotency-Key` or disable retry. We can add routing policy flags to mark which backends are resume-capable.
Maria: Agreed. Action items: - Sam: prototype Stream-Id + Idempotency-Key enforcement at edge (reject with 422 if streaming write lacks header). - Kevin: draft resume token RFC for internal backends (include trailer format + proxy contract). - Olivia: update routing config to include `resume_capable: true/false`. - Jun: add metrics and alert rule for duplicate-stream-detection.
Sam: I'll start a small proxy change: patch will check `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` OR `Content-Type: multipart/related` and require `X-Redwood-Stream-Id` for POST/PATCH/PUT that have `x-redwood-side-effect: true`. Sample config:```
route:
  resume_capable: false
  require_stream_id: true
```
Kevin: For the RFC I'll include this example trailer and server contract:```
--trailer
Content-Type: application/json
{ "resume_token": "sha256:...", "offset": 12345 }
```
Olivia: UX question — SDKs should auto-generate `Idempotency-Key` + `Stream-Id` and surface a `onResume` callback. Add to TODO.
Jun: I updated the alert: `sum(edge_requests{streaming=1, retries>0}) by (route)` and a new `edge_duplicate_inserts_total`.
deploy-bot: deploy 2024-09-12T15:04:00Z: edge-proxy@canary -> promoted to staging (sha: d4c3b2). :rocket:
Maria: Thanks. Let's reconvene after Kevin's RFC. If we can't support resume tokens for many upstreams, we default to explicit idempotency and no automatic retry for streams.
Sam: +1. I'll open the patch and a small e2e harness that simulates client midstream aborts.
Kevin: Will include performance notes — resume token checks add ~0.5ms p99 for streaming handshakes, but avoids db-level dedupe cost.
Olivia: One more: document what happens on partial delivery to downstreams (webhooks). We might need a separate webhook-safe mode.
Maria: Noted. Closing loop: I'll add a short doc in the Runbook about how to triage duplicate streaming writes and where to look in traces.
